about.title: About - Alexis
about.who_text: My name is Alexis, a 5th-year student at Epitech Montpellier, passionate about video game creation and innovative technologies. I had the opportunity to study at Saxion University of Applied Sciences in the Netherlands, an experience that opened my mind to new perspectives on development and international collaboration.
about.journey_intro: Here is an overview of my academic and professional background, which has allowed me to develop skills across different domains, contexts, and programming languages:
about.journey_epitech_text: As a 5th-year student at Epitech Montpellier, I joined this school to gain a solid foundation in software development. I took part in various individual and group projects using languages like C, C++, Python, and many others, strengthening my technical skills.
about.journey_saxion_text: During my 4th year at Epitech, I completed an international exchange at Saxion University (Netherlands), focused on video game development with Unity. I collaborated on group projects within multicultural teams, sharpening my game design and teamwork skills.
about.journey_odigo_text: At the end of my 1st year at Epitech, I completed an internship at Odigo Baillargues as a full-stack developer. Working alongside an overseas Odigo colleague, I built a website to streamline team project tracking, reinforcing my front-end and back-end development skills.
about.journey_seedship_title: Internship at The Seed Ship (February 2024 - May 2024)
about.journey_seedship_text: During my 3rd year, I completed an internship at The Seed Shop in Montpellier as a full-stack developer and DevOps. I worked with another Epitech student on a product launch project using tools such as Joomla, Laravel, Docker, and others.
about.journey_socle_text: Since the start of my 5th year, I have been interning at Socle AI as a full-stack AI developer. I carried out many AI-related tasks and fully built an AI Hackathon for Epitech Paris students using Unity WebGL - a board game where AI agents compete against each other.
about.journey_cgi_text: End-of-study internship as an integration developer, where I design MuleSoft flows that meet client requirements and assigned tickets, relying notably on DataWeave for data transformation. I also contribute to an internal project and actively take part in team and client follow-up meetings.
about.journey_cdi_title: Permanent position at CGI Montpellier (From Mid-October 2026)
about.journey_cdi_text: Continuing on from my end-of-study internship with a permanent position at CGI Montpellier.
about.skills_intro: After almost five years at Epitech, I have acquired strong skills across various programming languages and tools.
about.skill_c_desc: Low-level programming and memory management for high-performance projects.
about.skill_cpp_desc: High-performance software development and advanced resource management for complex applications.
about.skill_csharp_desc: Application and game mechanic development with Unity.
about.skill_unity_desc: Creation of immersive video games and interactive prototypes.
about.skill_docker_desc: Application containerization for efficient deployment and simplified environment management.
about.skill_python_desc: Scripting, automation, and versatile application development.
about.skill_mulesoft_desc: Application integration and data transformation using MuleSoft (Anypoint Platform) and the DataWeave language.
about.tools_intro: Beyond languages, here are the tools that are part of my daily developer workflow:
about.quality_passion_text: Video games have always been my passion. Being able to work in game development is truly fulfilling.
about.quality_team_text: My international experience taught me to collaborate effectively with diverse profiles.
about.quality_lead_text: As the technical reference on projects, I validated feasibility and coordinated the integration of features into the game.
about.gaming_text1: Since childhood, video games have always drawn me in. Thanks to my father, I discovered the early The Legend of Zelda, Mario, Pokémon games and many other iconic Nintendo titles.
about.gaming_text2: Today, that passion remains strong and accompanies my learning journey - not only in game development, but across other fields as well.
about.learning_intro: I believe a good developer never stops learning. Here's what I'm working on outside of class:
about.learning_unreal_text: Exploring Unreal Engine through a Pokémon x Unreal Engine project set in a 2.5D world.
about.learning_perso_text: Building small tools and games outside of studies to practice freely and explore new ideas without academic constraints.
about.learning_design_text: Deepening knowledge of game feel, level design, and balancing principles to better understand the mechanics that make a game fun.

projects.title: My Projects - Alexis
projects.intro: Discover my work in video game development and low-level programming, completed during my studies at Epitech and Saxion University, as well as my personal projects.

unitetools.name: Unite Tools
unitetools.desc1: Unite Tools is a fan-made website entirely dedicated to Pokémon Unite, developed and maintained by me outside of my studies.
unitetools.desc2: The site offers several handy tools for players: a draft simulator to prepare competitive matches, a customizable tierlist creator, a damage calculator, and more features in development (dynamic map, map timings).
unitetools.desc3: This project demonstrates my ability to design and maintain a web product solo from A to Z - from conception to deployment on GitHub Pages - while staying up to date with game patches and new content.
unitetools.desc4: Available in 5 languages: French, English, German, Spanish, Italian.
unitetools.short: A website dedicated to Pokémon Unite: draft simulator, tierlist creator, damage calculator and more. Fan-made project kept up to date.

pokemon_framework.name: Pokémon Unity Framework
pokemon_framework.desc1: An open-source Unity framework designed to help other developers build their own Pokémon-inspired games more easily: turn-based battle system, creature management, capture, inventory, save system...
pokemon_framework.desc2: The goal is to lay down a solid, reusable foundation - architecture, core systems - so other devs can focus on their game's content instead of the technical plumbing.
pokemon_framework.desc3: This framework also serves as the base for my own fangame, being developed alongside it.
pokemon_framework.short: Open-source Unity framework to help other developers build their own Pokémon-inspired games (battles, creatures, capture, save system).

pokemon_fangame.name: Pokémon Fangame
pokemon_fangame.desc1: My own Pokémon fangame, built in Unity on top of my personal framework. The goal is to deliver an original experience while digging deep into the genre's mechanics.
pokemon_fangame.desc2: This project lets me validate the framework's architecture choices in a real-world setting, while also working on game design, writing, and art direction for a complete game.
pokemon_fangame.desc3: More details to come as the project progresses.
pokemon_fangame.short: My personal Pokémon fangame, built in Unity on top of my own framework.

maskarena.name: MaskArena
maskarena.desc1: MaskArena is a local fighting game made in 48 hours during the Global Game Jam 2026, on-site at Brassart Montpellier school, around the imposed theme "Mask".
maskarena.desc2: The game features 2 to 4 player local combat (controllers recommended) where each player controls a doll that can equip up to 4 masks simultaneously. Each mask grants an active ability - jump, dash, attack, counter, etc. Without a mask, the character can only move.
maskarena.desc3: The core mechanic revolves around cooldown management: using a mask puts it on cooldown. Taking a hit also puts a mask on cooldown. If all your masks are on cooldown when you take a hit, you die. A simple system on paper, but one that creates constant tactical tension.
maskarena.desc4: As Lead Developer, I coordinated the technical decisions and supervised the integration of game mechanics in Unity within a team of 6.
maskarena.short: Local 2-4 player fighting game made in 48h. Play as a doll equipped with 4 masks, each granting a unique ability: jump, dash, attack, counter... Managing cooldowns is surviving.

epitech_jam.name: Epitech Jam & GGJ 2025
epitech_jam.desc: Two other game jam participations (internal Epitech Jam and Global Game Jam), formative experiences in rapid game creation.

little_monsters.name: Little Monsters
little_monsters.short: Unity game for children featuring AI and dynamic interactions.
little_monsters.desc1: This game was built with the Unity engine as part of a group project at Saxion University of Applied Sciences in the Netherlands.
little_monsters.desc2: I worked alongside game designers and 2D/3D artists to create a game aimed at young players, based on creatures imagined by children at a partner school.
little_monsters.desc3: The goal was to design a fun and accessible game faithful to the world invented by the children, while delivering a cohesive and enjoyable experience.
little_monsters.desc4: As a Unity developer, I handled gameplay programming, integration of 3D monster animations and their AI, world interactions, and the random spawning of monsters in their respective biomes.

shenanigans.name: Shenanigans
shenanigans.short: Unity multiplayer game using camera drawing and gyroscope.
shenanigans.desc1: This game was built with the Unity engine as part of a group project at Saxion University of Applied Sciences in the Netherlands.
shenanigans.desc2: I collaborated with game designers and artists to develop a multiplayer game (3 players) using the gyroscope features of mobile devices, with a PC as the host.
shenanigans.desc3: The goal was to create a fun and creative experience where each player, using their phone, receives a theme and a body part to draw within a time limit. The PC hosts the game and displays the final result by combining the drawings into a unique creature.
shenanigans.desc4: As a Unity developer, I implemented the phone-based drawing mechanic, multiplayer synchronisation between mobile devices and the PC, and real-time assembly of drawings on the host.

chasing_echoes.name: Chasing Echoes
chasing_echoes.short: Unity game raising awareness about forest fires through mini-games.
chasing_echoes.desc1: This game was built with the Unity engine as part of a group project at Saxion University of Applied Sciences in the Netherlands.
chasing_echoes.desc2: The goal of our project was to raise awareness about forest fire prevention through an engaging interactive experience.
chasing_echoes.desc3: The player takes on the role of a forest watchtower employee, tasked with monitoring the surroundings during a crisis. Distress calls come in from people lost in the forest, threatened by a spreading fire.
chasing_echoes.desc4: As a Unity developer, I contributed to the integration of mini-games, the logic for receiving and processing calls, and managing the progression of the fire on the map.

arcade.name: Arcade
arcade.short: C++ arcade game with dynamic switching between graphics libraries mid-game.
arcade.desc1: This project was built in C++ as part of my second year at Epitech.
arcade.desc2: I collaborated with a team of fellow students to develop an arcade game that works with interchangeable graphics libraries.
arcade.desc3: The goal was to create a smooth experience allowing dynamic switching between different graphics libraries (SFML, Stdlib, ncurses) mid-game while maintaining stable gameplay.
arcade.desc4: As a C++ developer, I implemented the graphics library management logic, dynamic transitions, and game-specific high score saving.

zappy.name: Zappy
zappy.short: Networked game in C (server), C++/Raylib (client) and Python3 (AI), focused on resource collection.
zappy.desc1: This project was completed during my second year at Epitech, in C, C++ and Python3.
zappy.desc2: I collaborated with a team of students to develop Zappy, a network game where teams compete to collect resources on a map.
zappy.desc3: The goal was to create a competitive experience with a robust C server, a C++/Raylib graphical client, and Python3 AI, aiming to get six players to the maximum level.
zappy.desc4: As a developer, I co-developed the character AI, implemented error handling, and wrote unit tests in C and C++.

shell.name: 42sh
shell.short: UNIX shell implementation in C, a command interpreter for UNIX systems, compiled via Makefile.
shell.desc1: This project was completed during my first year at Epitech, in the C language.
shell.desc2: I collaborated with a team of five students to develop 42sh, a command interpreter (shell) for UNIX systems.
shell.desc3: The goal was to create a robust and functional shell capable of executing complex UNIX commands, compiled via Makefile.
shell.desc4: As a developer, I implemented many shell features and commands, as well as unit tests to ensure its reliability.

tetris.name: Tetris
tetris.short: Tetris game in C using the ncurses library for a UNIX terminal interface, compiled via Makefile.
tetris.desc1: This project was completed during my second year at Epitech, in the C language.
tetris.desc2: I collaborated with a team to develop a Tetris game using the ncurses library for a UNIX terminal interface.
tetris.desc3: The goal was to recreate the classic Tetris gameplay with smooth controls and a text-based interface, compiled via Makefile.
tetris.desc4: As a developer, I implemented game mechanics, piece management, and user interactions.

zeldarogue.name: Zelda Rogue
zeldarogue.short: Zelda Rogue in C++, a turn-based game inspired by Pokerogue set in the Zelda universe, using the SFML graphics library.
zeldarogue.desc1: This project was completed during my fourth year at Saxion University, in C++.
zeldarogue.desc2: I developed Zelda Rogue solo: a turn-based game inspired by Pokérogue, but set in the Zelda universe with its iconic items and mechanics.
zeldarogue.desc3: The game features a leveling system, loot, and progressive difficulty, with combat using items with varied effects, all rendered through the SFML graphics library.
zeldarogue.desc4: As a solo developer, I designed and implemented all game mechanics, the turn-based system, and the graphical interface.

asm.name: ASM MiniLibC
asm.short: MiniLibC in ASM, implementing basic C functions (strlen, strchr, strcasecmp) for UNIX systems.
asm.desc1: This project was completed during my second year at Epitech, in assembly language (x86-64).
asm.desc2: Solo, I developed MiniLibC, a reimplementation of standard C library functions (strlen, memcpy, strcmp...) in assembly language.
asm.desc3: The goal was to gain a deeper understanding of low-level system calls and memory management, while respecting calling conventions in assembly.
asm.desc4: I also designed a unit test suite in C to rigorously validate the behaviour of each function, comparing my implementations against the standard libc.
